overview: Gasparinisaura cincosaltensis was a small ornithopod from the Late Cretaceous of Neuquén Province, Argentina (~83–80 Ma), about 1.7 metres long. Named after palaeontologist Zulma Gasparini, it is one of the best-documented small ornithopods from South America and helps fill a gap in our understanding of Late Cretaceous South American herbivore diversity.

A bonebed with multiple Gasparinisaura individuals has been found, providing bone histology data showing these animals were fast-growing and reached adult size within a few years — a growth strategy more similar to modern birds than to modern reptiles, consistent with the high metabolic rates now inferred for ornithischians generally.

fossilSites.name: Anacleto Formation
fossilSites.note: Late Cretaceous (Campanian) continental beds with multiple Gasparinisaura individuals including the type specimen.

articles.title: Discovery
articles.body: Rodolfo Coria and Leonardo Salgado described Gasparinisaura cincosaltensis in 1996 from Neuquén Province. The name honours Zulma Gasparini, a leading Argentine palaeontologist. The type specimen preserves skull and postcranial material; additional specimens from a bonebed extend the sample.

articles.title: Phylogenetic position
articles.body: Gasparinisaura's position within Ornithopoda is debated: some analyses place it near the base of the group, others closer to Thescelosaurus or to Iguanodontia. Its relatively primitive features — small size, simple teeth — are consistent with a basal position, but without a clearly diagnostic skull it is difficult to resolve.

articles.title: Growth biology
articles.body: Bone histology from multiple Gasparinisaura specimens shows rapid growth rates, with the animals reaching adult size within a few years. This pattern — more bird-like than reptile-like — is now recognised as widespread in ornithischians and supports the inference of elevated metabolic rates in non-avian dinosaurs generally.

fossilRecord.material: Partial skeletal material of a small ornithopod.
fossilRecord.evidence: Slender limb bones and ornithopod dentition identify it as a small cursorial herbivore in the southern dinosaur fauna.

consensusScope: diet, locomotion and major uncertainty wording

record.description: Gasparinisaura cincosaltensis was a small bipedal ornithopod from the Anacleto Formation of Patagonia. Several partial skeletons, including juveniles and cranial material, document a lightly built southern neornithischian usually placed in Elasmaria.
facts: More than one growth stage is known.
Leaf-shaped teeth support herbivory, but exact plants are unknown.
Older assignment to Hypsilophodontidae reflects a now-abandoned catch-all grouping.

review.ageReviewNote: The Anacleto Formation is Campanian; local horizons are not dated closely enough for a narrow species range.
